questions: Is the goal to sort the permutation into ascending order (1, 2, ..., N) specifically, or just any ascending order (i.e., sorted order of the values present)?
When multiple swaps are possible, can we choose any sequence of swaps, or must we follow a specific algorithm (e.g., bubble sort)?
Is the cost incurred each time we perform a swap, or is it a one-time cost per chosen i? The operation says 'pay a cost of i, and swap P_i and P_{i+1}'.
Does the cost i refer to the index i in the current permutation before the swap, or the fixed position i in the original indexing (1..N)?
Are we allowed to perform swaps that temporarily make the permutation less sorted, as long as we eventually reach sorted order?
Should we output the minimum possible total cost, or just any total cost that results from some sequence of operations that sorts P?
If multiple minimal-cost sequences exist, do we output that minimal cost, or could any cost from a sorting sequence be acceptable?
Is the operation allowed only on adjacent elements, or after swapping, can we choose new adjacent pairs based on updated positions?
